text:
Plan: vertical cylinder on the z axis, all in **metres**. Barrel r=0.045 from z=0 to 0.120; 12 fins (r=0.070, t=0.003, pitch 0.009) centred on the barrel → stack 0.102 tall, from z=0.009 to 0.111; hemispherical head r=0.045 capping z=0.120..0.165. Duct 0.3×0.3 from z=-0.150 to z=0.465. Fluid = duct minus solid; the duct box will come from blockMesh (inlet/outlet/ductWalls as blockMesh patches) and snappyHexMesh will cut the cylinder in, but I still export all six STLs. First, the solid and its numbers.

```python
import os, subprocess
from build123d import *

R_B, H_B = 0.045, 0.120          # barrel radius, height
R_F, T_F, GAP, N_F = 0.070, 0.003, 0.006, 12   # fin radius, thickness, gap, count
PITCH = T_F + GAP
STACK = N_F*T_F + (N_F-1)*GAP
Z0 = (H_B - STACK)/2             # first fin bottom

barrel = Cylinder(R_B, H_B, align=(Align.CENTER, Align.CENTER, Align.MIN))
fins = [Pos(0,0,Z0+i*PITCH) * Cylinder(R_F, T_F, align=(Align.CENTER,Align.CENTER,Align.MIN)) for i in range(N_F)]
dome = Sphere(R_B) & Box(3*R_B, 3*R_B, R_B, align=(Align.CENTER,Align.CENTER,Align.MIN))
head = Pos(0,0,H_B) * dome

solid = barrel
for f in fins: solid = solid + f
solid = solid + head

bb = solid.bounding_box()
print("stack height", STACK, "first fin z", Z0, "last fin top", Z0+(N_F-1)*PITCH+T_F)
print("bbox", bb.min, bb.max, "vol", solid.volume)
print("n faces", len(solid.faces()))
```
Face classification matches the analytic areas exactly (head 2πR²=0.012723, fins 12×0.019383=0.232604, barrel 2πR·0.084+πR²=0.030112). Now the duct faces and the six STL exports.
Wall areas 0.3×0.615 ✓. Background hex mesh at 15 mm, with inlet/outlet/ductWalls as blockMesh patches (exact planar duct boundary).
Coarse snappy first: surface level 2 (3.75 mm) just to confirm the cut and patch naming, before refining into the 6 mm gaps.
Meshed at 46 k cells. Look at it: a y=0 slice of the mesh plus the patch surfaces.
Shape is right (barrel red between fins, dome green, duct/inlet/outlet named). The 6 mm gaps are only ~1 cell wide at level 2 — refine to level 3 (1.875 mm, 3 cells per gap).
snappy ran on the already-snapped mesh (`-overwrite` replaced it) — rebuild the background mesh first.
Mesh OK. Volume check: 0.3²×0.615 − solid 0.00127941 = 0.0540706 vs mesh 0.054071 ✓. Now verify patch areas against the analytic values and count cells across a fin gap.

Everything checks out numerically:

| quantity | asked | measured on the built geometry/mesh |
|---|---|---|
| barrel OD × height | 90 mm × 120 mm | patch r_max 0.04507 m (snapped facets), z 0…0.120 m |
| fins | 12, OD 140 mm, t 3 mm, gap 6 mm | 12 by construction; fin patch r 0.045…0.07003 m, stack z 0.009…0.111 m = 12×3 + 11×6 mm |
| fin patch area | 12×(2π(0.07²−0.045²)+2π·0.07·0.003)=0.232604 m² | 0.232577 m² (−0.01 %) |
| barrel patch area | 2π·0.045·0.084 + π·0.045² = 0.030112 m² | 0.030101 m² |
| head | hemispherical dome closing top | spherical face r=0.045, z 0.120…0.165, area 0.012720 vs 2πR²=0.012723 m² |
| duct | 300×300, 150 below / 300 above | bbox (−0.15,−0.15,−0.15)…(0.15,0.15,0.465); inlet/outlet 0.09 m² each, walls 0.738 m² |
| fluid volume | duct − solid = 0.0540706 m³ | checkMesh total 0.054071 m³ |

Built in metres throughout (no STEP import, so no unit scaling was needed). Six STLs written to `constant/triSurface` before meshing — `barrel.stl`, `fins.stl`, `head.stl`, `head`/`ductWalls.stl`, `inlet.stl`, `outlet.stl` — with the patch names decided from intrinsic face geometry (sphere → head, cylinder r=45 mm and the closed base → barrel, r=70 mm rims + annular flanks → fins), never from bounding-box position. The duct boundary comes from blockMesh so inlet/outlet/ductWalls are exact planes; snappyHexMesh only cuts the cylinder in. Final mesh 256 476 cells (92 % hex), surface level 3 → 3–4 cells across each 6 mm fin gap; `checkMesh` says **Mesh OK** (max non-orthogonality 48.2, max skewness 2.82).

Not checked: no boundary layers were added (`addLayers false`), so near-wall spacing is the cut-cell size, not a y⁺ target; and I did not verify each of the 12 fins individually in the mesh — the count rests on the construction plus the total fin area matching 12 fins to 0.01 %.
